DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE HON. MAGTANGGOL T. GUNIGUNDO I 2nd District, Valenzuela City Room 21 2, North Wing Batasan Complex, Diliman Quezon City Dear Congressman Gunigundo: DILG Legal Opinion No. 29 s. 2012 APR 13 2012 LOCAL CENTRAL RECOROS' SECT'ON REL E A s,eo SIGNATURE DATE: TIME! This has reference to your letter dated 02 April 2012 interposing a query on this issue: "When does the corporate existence of a barangay begin?" In reply thereto, may we invite your attention to Section 14 of the Local Government Code (RA 71 60) which provides that: "SEC. 14. Beginning of Corporate Existence.- When a new local government unit is created, its corporate existence shall commence upon the election and qualification of its chief executive and a majority of the members of its sanggunian, unless some other time is fixed therefor by the law or ordinance creating it." The aforequoted provision of Section 14 of the Local Government Code provides for the general rule that the corporate existence of a local government unit, including barangays, shall commence upon the election and qualification of its chief executive and a majority of the members of its sanggunian. Said provision, however, is immediately followed by an exception, i.e., "unless some other time is fixed therefor by the law or ordinance creating it". Hence, if the law or ordinance creating a new local government unit is silent as to the time or period when its corporate existence shall commence, then the aforequoted Section 14 of the Local Government Code shall govern. On the other hand, if the law or ordinance creating a new local government unit provides some other time (other than that provided under Section 14 of the Local Government Code), then the corporate existence of the local government unit commences at such time. In DILG Opinion No. 34, series of 2007, we had the opportunity to cite one example where the corporate existence of a local government unit was set at the time other than that provided under Section 14 of the Local Government Code. As represented therein, Sections 49 and 50 of RA 9355 (An Act Creating the Province of Dinagat Island) provide that: U SEC. 49. Commencement of Corporate Existence.- The Province of Dinagat Islands shall commence its corporate existence upon the election and qualification of the governor, vice governor and majority of the members of the sangguniang panlalawigan. " "SEC. 50. Officials of the Province of Dinagat Islands.- (A) The first set of elective officials of the Province of Dinagat Islands shall be elected in the next local elections following the effectivity of this Act.

The President of the Philippines shall appoint an interim governor, vice governor and members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, who shall serve only until a new set of provincial officials have been elected and qualified. " We opined therein that the corporate existence of the Province of Dinagat Islands should be reckoned from the appointment by the President of the interim set of local elective officials thereat. Pertinent portion of DILG Opinion No. 34, series of 2007 provides: 'xxx Section 49 of RA 9355 provides for the general rule with respect to the commencement of corporate existence of the Province of Dinagat Islands which was also the general rule found in Section 14 of the Local Government Code. Section 50 of RA 9355, however, provided for the transitory provision where the President was empowered by the law itself to appoint the interim governor, vice governor and members of the sangguniang panlalawigan who shall serve only until a new set of provincial officials have been elected and qualified. This is understandable because under the first paragraph of Section 50 of RA 9355, it is mandated that the first set of elective officials of the province shall be elected in the next local elections following the effectivity of the Act. Corollarily, since the Act was approved on 02 October 2006 and the subsequent plebiscite was conducted which resulted to its ratification, the logical conclusion would be that the first set of elective local officials shall be elected come 14 May 2007 elections. At this point, it bears to state the doctrinal pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the case of "Mejia CS. (81 Phil. 486), where the court ruled that the City of Dagupan came into existence as a legal entity or public corporation upon approval of said Act creating it. But as a city is a public corporation or a juridical entity, and as such cannot operate or transact business by itself but through its agents or officers, it was necessary that the officials thereof be appointed or elected in order that it may act or transact business as such public corporation or city. The Supreme Court saw the necessity that the city government be organized since according to the highest court, to create a public corporation is one thing and to organize the government thereof is another. With the Supreme Court pronouncement in the aforecited case, taken along with the exception provided under Section 14 of the Local Government Code, it does becomes obvious that the intention of Congress in empowering the President to appoint the set of interim elective local officials of Dinagat Islands pending the election of the first set of its local elective officials in the next local elections following the effectivity of the law creating the province is to confer upon the province its immediate corporate existence so that the province can already normally operate as a political subdivision of the State bestowed with corporate and governmental powers for the benefit of its constituents. This is the common purpose that could be seen in harmonizing Section 14 of the Local Government Code and Sections 49 and 50 of RA 9355. The conferment unto the President of the power to appoint the interim set of local elective officials should be taken as an exception to the general rule found in Section 14 of the Local Government Code."(Emphasis Supplied) We hope the foregoing addresses your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, JESUS B. QU Director Ill Ls/17
